Why your PDF is not getting smaller

By Sarvesh Singh · Updated 20 October 2026

A PDF can contain text instructions, images, fonts and document structure. Which part occupies the most space determines whether a particular optimization method can help. “Compress PDF” is not one operation that works equally well for every file.

What this optimizer actually changes

Optimize PDF rewrites the document structure using object streams. It does not reduce the resolution of scanned pages or recompress every embedded photo. A text-based PDF with inefficient structure may shrink; a PDF whose size mostly comes from scanned images may change very little.

A concrete example

Imagine a 10 MB document where approximately 9.5 MB is scanned image data and 0.5 MB is other structure. Even removing all of that structure—which a valid PDF still needs—would not reduce the file below 9.5 MB if the images stay unchanged. This is an illustrative calculation, not a measured claim about your file or a promised compression result.

Try the behavior safely

Download the two-page practice PDF, then select it in Optimize PDF. It is already small, so do not expect a large reduction. Compare the reported output size with the input. If rewriting makes it the same size or larger, yourPDF offers the unchanged original and says so. A successful operation is not always a smaller file.

Choose the next step based on the document

  • A scan you created: return to the scanner or source document and export at an appropriate resolution and quality. Check fine print, signatures and stamps before accepting reduced quality.
  • Unnecessary pages: use Remove pages only when the recipient does not require them. Removing content is different from compressing it.
  • A report you authored: optimize large source images and re-export from the authoring application. Keep text selectable where possible.
  • An already compact PDF: leave it unchanged unless there is a real size requirement. A conversion through JPG can remove searchable text and accessibility information.

Before submitting a smaller PDF

Open the output, check every page, and compare small text and images with the original. Verify the exact byte limit stated by the receiving service. This tool cannot guarantee a target such as 100 KB, and any edit can invalidate digital signatures. Keep original signed documents.

Need only part of a document?

Extract pages saves selected pages into a new PDF. Split PDF can create separate files. Neither option means a portal will accept multiple uploads; follow its instructions. For supported limits and document features that may change, read Help & limits.
